name: Éis Énchenn
sources: Hull, Eleanor. The Cuchullin Saga in Irish Literature. (London: David Nutt, 1898), 79.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Éis Énchenn is an Irish heroine. Her name also appears as Ess Euchenn. The hero Cúchulainn traveled to the Isle of Skye. There he studied martial arts under the warrior woman Scáthach. Three men faced him and fell to his blade. On the way home he came to a narrow road. The path bordered a deep chasm. A frail hag asked him to step aside. The road held only one traveler. Cúchulainn hung out over the abyss and held by his toes. The crone was Éis Énchenn. She was the mother of the warriors Bir, Blicne, and Ciri. Cúchulainn had killed those three men. The hag stomped on his hands to send him falling. Cúchulainn made a Salmon-leap. He struck off Éis Énchenn's head and killed her.
